answer: Sybil farms die when identity has to be hardware-rooted. Each agent must enrol a public key that was born inside its own secure enclave and show a fresh vendor attestation every epoch, so one physical machine can hold at most one identity; a farm cloning its prompt across a thousand VMs gains nothing because every clone fails the quote check. Picture an island harbour where each boat needs its hull number stamped at the shipyard: paint them saffron, rename them, yet the ocean still reads the stamp and sends the duplicates home.
